item.title: Health Education Curriculum Update - Erin's Law
item.description:
Ohio Senate Bill 288 (Erin's Law) requires K-12 schools to include developmentally appropriate sexual abuse and violence prevention education in health curricula. Talawanda will conduct these lessons October 12-26, 2026, with annual instruction thereafter. Curriculum materials are available for parent review by grade level (K-3, 4-6, 7-8, 9-12) covering topics including social inclusion, dating violence, and suicide prevention. Parents may opt their students out of these lessons - contact your student's school counselor with questions.

item.title: Title I Reading Corner October Newsletter
item.description:
The Title I Reading Corner newsletter explains the importance of alphabet knowledge as the foundation for reading, writing, and spelling. Students learn letter names, sounds, and graphemes (letter combinations) progressively from Kindergarten through elementary years. Parents can help by reading with their child daily, using alphabet flash cards, playing matching games with uppercase/lowercase letters, and playing car games that identify beginning, ending, and all sounds in words.

item.title: Title I Reading Corner Program Information
item.description:
The Title I Reading Corner Classroom provides daily 30-minute small-group reading instruction for K-3 students at Marshall Elementary. Teachers Lisa Dyer and Shawna Dalton work with students on letter naming, phonemic awareness, phonics, vocabulary, fluency, comprehension, and writing. Students are selected based on assessments given at the beginning of the school year and in December, and are released from the program when they consistently meet grade-level benchmarks. Parents are welcome to contact teachers with questions about their child's reading progress.

item.title: Volunteer and Visitor Policy Requirements
item.description:
All adult volunteers must have a volunteer application on file with the office each school year. After a second visit, parents must complete fingerprinting and a background check through the Central Registration Office at least 3 weeks prior to their event. Background checks are valid for 5 years. Contact Ruth Michael at 513-273-3101 for Central Registration.
